Each runs its own Health Information Management department with its own phone, fax, and email, so a request sent to the wrong location is an easy way to end up with a "records not found" response. For Texas personal injury firms, knowing the right form, the right contact, and how fees work is the difference between records in a couple of weeks and a file that sits.[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) offers AI-powered medical record retrieval that validates authorizations before submission and manages persistent follow-up across all of those locations.

-


Houston Methodist lists nine hospital facilities, plus the Physician Organization for clinic and outpatient records


-


The authorization for non-patient requests is Form HM2351, one page, Version 6, dated January 2025, valid for 180 days unless another period is specified


-


A patient requesting their own records uses a Patient Access Request rather than the HM2351 disclosure authorization


-


Texas law imposes a 15-business-day access requirement in defined patient-access circumstances; HIPAA generally allows up to 30 calendar days subject to one permitted extension


-


Hospital record fees are governed by Texas Health and Safety Code § 241.154 and HHSC guidance, which differ from the Texas Medical Board's physician schedule


-

## **Understanding the Houston Methodist Medical Records Request Process**


Houston Methodist provides several request channels: an online form, a downloadable Patient Access form, MyChart, telephone contact, and mail, fax, or email submission. Requests route through the Health Information Management department at each facility.


Which form you need depends on who's asking. A patient exercising the HIPAA right of access generally submits a Patient Access Request rather than a disclosure authorization. When the requester is someone other than the patient, including a law firm, Houston Methodist provides[Form HM2351](https://www.houstonmethodist.org/medical-records/) , "Authorization for Use and Disclosure of Health Information," completed by the patient or an appropriate guardian or legal representative. HM2351 says the signer will be asked for proof of identity and, where applicable, guardianship or other authority.


For law firms, the authorization is the checkpoint. Incomplete or defective authorizations are a leading preventable cause of rejected requests, and a returned form means starting over. Codes Health's AI review catches these errors before submission, flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that otherwise cause rejections.

Anything outside MyChart goes through Health Information Management, which can confirm what remains available and in what format.

That range helps locate records even when a client's recollection is incomplete.


## **Houston Methodist Hospital Medical Records Request Form: Essential Details**


Form HM2351, "Authorization for Use and Disclosure of Health Information," is a one-page document, Version 6, dated January 2025, available as a download or through online DocuSign versions specific to each hospital location.


### **Downloading the Official Release Form**


Get the authorization through:


-


The[Houston Methodist medical](https://www.houstonmethodist.org/medical-records/) records webpage


-


Direct DocuSign links for each hospital location


-


The[Texas Attorney General's](https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/sites/default/files/files/divisions/consumer-protection/hb300-Authorization-Disclose-Health-Info.pdf) standard authorization form, designed to comply with Texas medical privacy requirements; covered entities may use it or another compliant form


### **Completing the Request Form Accurately**


Complete every applicable field to avoid a rejection:


**Patient Identification:** full legal name including maiden name if applicable, date of birth, and current mailing address and telephone number


**Authorization Parties:** the "to disclose/release" field with the specific facility, and the "to receive" field with recipient name, address, phone, and fax


**Health Information to Be Disclosed:** check all applicable record types, including the complete medical record, operative reports, history and physical, discharge summary, consultation reports, radiology reports, laboratory results, and ER records. HM2351 also lets you separately select radiology films, pathology slides or blocks, fetal monitoring strips, photographs, and billing records, so request those explicitly and confirm formats with HIM.


**Dates of Service:** specify exact date ranges, since vague requests invite incomplete responses.


**Sensitive information:** this is where the two Texas forms differ, and mixing them up causes problems. HM2351 has no separate initial lines for HIV/AIDS, mental health, or substance use information; it states that information released may include those categories. The Texas AG's standard form does have initial lines for mental health, substance abuse, genetic information, and HIV/AIDS. Check which form you're completing before assuming initials are required.


Codes Health validates requests before submission, checking authorizations, date ranges, and provider-specific requirements.


## **HIPAA Authorization Form for Houston Methodist: Ensuring Compliance**


HIPAA requires specific elements in any valid authorization for release of protected health information. Houston Methodist's form meets them, but completion errors remain common.


### **Specifics for Family Members and Representatives**


Two different situations carry different requirements:


-


**A patient-authorized recipient** , including an adult family member named on the authorization, needs no independent legal authority. The patient's authorization is what permits the disclosure.


-


**A personal representative acting without a separate patient authorization** , such as a guardian, executor, or holder of a medical power of attorney, may be required to document that authority.


Houston Methodist also offers MyChart proxy access, which an adult patient can approve directly.


For a deceased patient, contact Houston Methodist to determine what documentation establishes the requester's legal authority, such as executor or estate documentation. A death certificate may also be requested, but it does not by itself establish authority to obtain the records.


### **Common Mistakes to Avoid on HIPAA Forms**


-


**Missing or incomplete signature:** the form must be properly signed. Houston Methodist states that a photocopy or fax of the signed authorization is valid as the original.


-


**Assuming you must write in an expiration:** HM2351 is valid for 180 days unless a different period is specified


-


**Applying the wrong form's sensitive-record rules:** see the distinction above between HM2351 and the Texas AG form


-


**Wrong recipient information:** double-check attorney name, firm address, and fax numbers


-


**Expired authorization:** forms submitted well after signing may be rejected


Codes Health manages authorization workflows end to end, including signature collection, while respecting each facility's requirements.

## **How to Request Medical Records from Houston Methodist Online or via MyChart**


### **Navigating Houston Methodist MyChart for Records**


MyChart is the fastest self-service option for patients:


1.


Go to mychart.houstonmethodist.org or use the MyMethodist app


2.


Log in or create an account (requires identity verification)


3.


Open "Medical Records" or "Health Summary"


4.


Select date range and record types


5.


Download records as PDF files


MyChart gives immediate access to what's already in the portal, subject to the historical limits above.


### **Digital Submission Best Practices**


For online DocuSign submissions:


-


Select the correct hospital location from the medical records webpage


-


Complete all required fields before submitting


-


Have identification ready, since proof of identity and, where applicable, legal authority may be required


-


Save the confirmation email for tracking


Electronic submission avoids postal delivery time and may reduce routing delays. As a firm workflow practice, not hospital policy, diary a follow-up call if nothing comes back within your expected window.


## **Ensuring Completeness: What to Expect After Requesting Houston Methodist Records**


### **Typical Turnaround Times**


Texas law imposes a 15-business-day requirement in defined patient-access circumstances. The Texas Attorney General states that where a provider's electronic records system can fulfill the request, records must be provided by the 15th business day after a written patient request, and Texas Occupations Code § 159.006 imposes a 15-business-day obligation on physicians after a qualifying written request. HIPAA generally allows up to 30 calendar days with one permitted extension, though a shorter state deadline can control.


Those are access rules in defined circumstances, not a blanket deadline for every attorney request. Houston Methodist publishes no general processing range, so delivery depends on:


-


Submission method


-


Record volume and complexity


-


Whether the records are readily available


-


Completeness of the authorization


### **Checking for Missing Documents or Information**


Before closing a retrieval, verify you received all dates of service listed in the authorization, both clinical notes and billing records, operative reports if surgery occurred, radiology and imaging reports, and discharge summaries for all admissions.


Cross-referencing billing against received records helps surface potential gaps, but discrepancies don't necessarily prove clinical records are missing. Separate professional billing, bundled services, ancillary providers, and coding conventions complicate the reconciliation.


Codes Health checks delivered records against the original request and works with facilities to resolve gaps before returning the set, which helps firms judge whether the documentation is genuinely complete.


## **Request Medical Records for Legal Cases Involving Houston Methodist**


### **Legal Authorizations vs. Standard Patient Requests**


Attorney requests differ from patient requests in a few ways:


-


**Fees:** charges depend on the request and applicable federal and Texas law. HIPAA permits a reasonable, cost-based fee for copies requested under the[right of access](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/privacy/guidance/access/index.html) , subject to strict limits. Hospital charges fall under Texas Health and Safety Code § 241.154, with maximum-fee guidance from[Texas HHSC](https://www.hhs.texas.gov/sites/default/files/documents/hospital-medical-record-fees.pdf) . Those rules differ from the[Texas Medical Board's](https://www.tmb.texas.gov/305-what-are-reasonable-fees-medical-records) physician schedule, so don't apply physician-office rates here.


-


**Certification:** trial admissibility may require a Custodian of Records Affidavit. The Medical Board allows a physician up to $15 for executing one; hospital records fall under a different framework allowing a reasonable certification charge within the applicable limit, so confirm the amount.


-


**Payment timing:** HM2351 states that any payment is due before or at the time of disclosure.


-


**Scope:** legal requests often span longer timeframes and more record types.


### **Processing Records for Medical Malpractice or Personal Injury**


For litigation support, firms commonly:


-


Consider a period of pre-incident records to establish baseline health, with the scope depending on the claims, defenses, relevance, proportionality, and discovery rules


-


Include follow-up treatment through physical therapy, specialists, and ongoing care


-


Obtain billing separately with CPT codes for damages documentation


-


Request certification when trial admissibility requires it

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How long does it take to get medical records from Houston Methodist Hospital?**


Texas law imposes a 15-business-day access requirement in defined patient-access circumstances, and HIPAA generally allows up to 30 calendar days with one permitted extension, though a shorter state deadline can control. Houston Methodist publishes no general processing range on its[medical records page](https://www.houstonmethodist.org/medical-records/) . Electronic submission avoids postal delivery time. ### **Can a family member request my medical records from Houston Methodist?**


Yes, in two ways. An adult family member the patient names on a valid authorization can receive records without independent legal authority. Separately, a guardian, executor, or holder of a medical power of attorney may act as a personal representative and can be asked to document that authority. Houston Methodist may require proof of identity and, where applicable, guardianship or other authority. MyChart proxy access is a third route an adult patient can approve directly.


### **Is there a fee to request medical records from Houston Methodist?**


Fees depend on the request and applicable federal and Texas law. HIPAA limits patient-access charges to certain reasonable, cost-based expenses. Hospital charges are governed by Texas Health and Safety Code § 241.154 and HHSC maximum-fee guidance, which differ from the Texas Medical Board's physician schedule, so don't apply physician-office rates here. Houston Methodist's forms state that fees may apply and payment is due before or at the time of disclosure, so confirm charges with the facility.


### **What if I need my Houston Methodist medical records urgently for an emergency?**


Treating providers should use Houston Methodist's own physician record-access channels, including EpicCare Link for qualifying professionals, rather than a general fax protocol. For legal deadlines, work in parallel: submit the formal request immediately, have your client pull what's available through MyChart, and call HIM to explain the urgency. Codes Health's retrieval timeline of a couple of weeks gives firms a buffer.


### **What records should I request for a personal injury case involving Houston Methodist?**


Request the complete medical record, operative and procedure reports, diagnostic imaging reports, laboratory results, ER records, discharge summaries, consultation reports, and itemized billing with CPT codes. Radiology films and pathology slides or blocks are separate selections on HM2351, so ask for them explicitly and confirm the delivery format. Pre-incident records can help establish baseline health, with the scope depending on the claims, defenses, and applicable discovery rules. Billing may be processed separately from clinical documentation.
